director.chapterArc: Tactical instruction shifts to combat panic and realization, ending in a somber debrief where tactical knowledge is distinguished from execution under fear.
director.restraintNote: Maintain the narrator's analytical distance. Do not dramatize Toren's internal failure; let the physical consequences (cold spike, inability to lift arms) carry the weight of his shame rather than emotional narration.

cues.delivery: Rook's instructional voice: flat, economical, and rhythmic. Treat the description of Stilts as a mechanical briefing rather than horror exposition.
cues.from: "Stilts, is what I call them. They stand about as high as me, and about nine-tenths of it is leg. Two legs, jointed backwards, longer than they've any business being, and a body slung between them no bigger than a dog, and a head you won't be able to find and won't need to. Colour of wet ash, same as the hounds, same as everything.
cues.through: "Stand where the trees are. Never stand at the end of a row. If you find yourself looking down a long clear stretch of anything, you are already in the wrong place, and you should move before you finish the thought."
cues.reason: Establishes Rook's authority and the tactical doctrine before action begins.

cues.delivery: Accelerate slightly into Toren's urgent internal monologue and the immediate action. Keep the description of Rook's strike clinical and precise.
cues.from: "Right," he said. "One right, in the hedge, it's gone still, it's choosing — it's going to come and it's coming right, everybody right—"
cues.through: Toren caught that part in pieces, out of order, and had to sort them afterward. Rook's weight had already gone onto the forward foot before the hound cleared the hedge. The light came out along the outside of his right forearm and took its edge on the way, from the wrist outward, the way a crack takes across ice. Then the arm went across at hip height. Once. Level. Without hurry.
cues.reason: Captures the shift from theory to practice; the violence is sudden but described without melodrama.

cues.delivery: Shift back to Toren's internal state: the ringing ears and chest expansion. Convey a quiet inflation of confidence that foreshadows the error.
cues.from: Milo was laughing in the high way he had when he had been frightened. "He called it. Tor called it before it moved."
cues.through: He did not say anything else. Toren walked the next two miles with his ears ringing and his chest about four inches further out than it had started the morning, and every step of those two miles laid down a little more of the thing that was going to cost them at four o'clock.
cues.reason: Sets up the psychological trap; the narrator must show this is dangerous ground for Toren.

cues.delivery: Rapid-fire tactical calls. The Ember activation should feel physical and mundane ('warm spike'), not magical or wondrous.
cues.from: "Third row, two of them, third row!" — Dessa, from the steps, clear and hard.
cues.through: Then the row discipline worked, and it worked so well that it was almost boring.
cues.reason: Maintains the rhythm of combat; Toren's confidence is high but grounded in sensory detail.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal error: 'He went to it instead of letting it come.' The narration must feel the mistake as a physical misstep in logic.
cues.from: He went to it instead of letting it come. That was the mistake, and he knew it while he did it. The first thrust went in under the slung body and came out with nothing on it. The second skidded off the top of the haunch; he had his weight forward on the front foot and could not turn with the thing when the thing turned. It came round on its planted point. That put him outside the trunk line, in the open, with the whole clear length of the fourth row standing at his back.
cues.through: By the time Toren had the rest of the sentence out, nobody stood in the row behind him.
cues.reason: The turning point where Toren breaks his own training; the narrator observes this failure objectively.

cues.delivery: Dessa's call: sharp and detached. Toren's realization of the ditch is frantic but internal; do not let it become a panic scream.
cues.from: She said it in a completely different voice from the one she had been using, and it went across the orchard like a thrown stone.
cues.through: "Down!" Rook shouted, from somewhere up the slope. "Everyone west — press-house — now, go, go—"
cues.reason: The scene shifts from controlled killing to chaos; the narrator must bridge this without losing control.

cues.delivery: Toren's activation: 'The world went very simple.' The description of the spike changing is clinical and terrifyingly efficient.
cues.from: "Right!" he shouted. "It's chosen — it's going right, it's committed right, turn right, everybody right—"
cues.through: He felt it go. It ran out of his fist in one clean movement — thinner, half again as long, the edge arriving before the length had finished arriving — and it was not ugly at all. The light did not stop at his knuckles this time. It went back up over his wrist and took the whole of his forearm, and the world went very simple.
cues.reason: This is the climax of action; the narrator must describe the release of power without romanticizing it.

cues.delivery: The aftermath: Toren's collapse and Wyck's intervention. The description of the impact on Wyck is physical ('water comes off a gatepost'), not heroic.
cues.from: There was nothing at all. The bottom came out of him the way the bottom comes out of a wet sack.
cues.through: He should have. Nine stone of boy, and a thing that had crossed forty feet in no time at all, and it came off him the way water comes off a gatepost. Wyck's boots stood exactly where Wyck's boots had been standing. The clay under them did not even give.
cues.reason: Shifts from high action to immediate consequence; focus on the physical reality of the injury.

cues.delivery: Rook's revelation: 'That's Ember.' The delivery must be flat and factual; Rook is explaining a mechanism, not praising a hero.
cues.from: "Two of them hit you at full run and you're standing where you were standing."
cues.through: "They'll never put you in a book for it. You can't show it to anybody. You can only be it, and you have been being it since before I met you, and it's the least impressive and most useful thing on this hillside."
cues.reason: The thematic core of the chapter; Wyck's passive ability is treated as mundane utility.

cues.delivery: The debrief: Rook's voice is tired and matter-of-fact. The final line 'Both of them are trainable' must land without a pause that suggests finality.
cues.through: "Both of them are trainable," said Rook. "That's all. Go to sleep."
cues.reason: Ends the chapter on an open-ended truth; avoid melodrama in the resolution.

pauses.after: "So don't watch them. Watch the lines."
pauses.reason: Completed thought: The core tactical doctrine is established.

pauses.after: Toren had gone to sleep with his hand on a warm stone thinking that this was the easiest thing anyone had ever asked him to remember.
pauses.reason: Transition from instruction to the morning's reality; a breath before action begins.

pauses.after: He did not say anything else. Toren walked the next two miles with his ears ringing and his chest about four inches further out than it had started the morning, and every step of those two miles laid down a little more of the thing that was going to cost them at four o'clock.
pauses.reason: Emotional landing: Toren's inflated confidence is noted as dangerous foreshadowing.
Speaker reset and tactical positioning; a moment of stillness before the fight starts.

pauses.after: "Two in the row, one at forty," Toren said after him, and got the spike out.
pauses.reason: Continuation: The spike comes up immediately after Toren identifies the target.

pauses.after: She said it in a completely different voice from the one she had been using, and it went across the orchard like a thrown stone.
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing: Dessa's call changes the scene from routine to crisis; listener needs time for the threat shift.

pauses.after: The first came straight up the middle. Milo called it at thirty feet. Toren set his feet the way he had been made to set them four hundred times. He did not go to meet it. The spike went in under the body as the body arrived. The thing's own weight finished it. The same weight put Toren flat on his back with a wasp-smelling mat of grass in his ear.
pauses.reason: Completed thought: The first kill is described clinically; a beat before Rook's action.

pauses.after: Toren's whole spine went cold. The cold came with a name already on it. The name was a gift. It was the wrong gift, and it was his.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and realization: Toren sees the foot print; a moment of dread before his error.
Major emotional landing: The exhaustion hits immediately after the kill; the world goes simple and empty.

pauses.after: He should have. Nine stone of boy, and a thing that had crossed forty feet in no time at all, and it came off him the way water comes off a gatepost. Wyck's boots stood exactly where Wyck's boots had been standing. The clay under them did not even give.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset: Wyck's impact is described physically; a pause to let the reality of his immunity sink in.

pauses.after: Rook let go of the arm.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: Rook shifts from tending the wound to explaining Wyck's nature; a reset for the new topic.
Completed thought: The agreement on borrowing Ember is final; transition to the debrief setting.
